issue_context.title: systemctl clean does not clean private directories but it does clean symlinks to them
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
> ... 243rc1

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released systemd versions upstream! -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > …Fedora Rawhide

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > …no cleaning of /var/lib/private/myapp

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > …cleaning of /var/lib/myapp (symlink)

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
systemd-run -p DymanicUser=yes -p User=joe -p CacheDirectory=joe /usr/bin/bash -c 'echo joe > /var/cache//joe/joe'
systemctl clean
ls /var/cache/joe /var/cache/private/joe

review_comments: hmm, an alternative might be two unconditionally delete both the regular and the private dir. Sounds like it would be more robust during updates?
